Some designs cannot be cropped, for example a poster with text on every edge or a product shot that must stay complete. Stretching a 3:2 poster into a 9:16 Story squeezes faces, warps logos and makes type look amateur; it is the one thing viewers notice immediately. Smart crop keeps the pixels undistorted: the image is scaled until it covers the target size and the overflow is cut away. The weakness of automatic cropping is that it usually cuts around the center, which is rarely where the subject is. That is what the focal point solves. Drag the dot onto the face, the product or the headline in the source thumbnail and every format, square, portrait, landscape and vertical, keeps that point inside the frame. When one placement still needs a nudge, open its preview and drag the image or zoom in; the override applies only to that format and is remembered until you reset it.
